pages.name: Bowlbug (Rock)
pages.source_text:
The '''Bowlbugs''' are a group of normal {{2|Monsters|Enemies}} found in the {{2|Hive}}. Each encounter features a Bowlbug (Rock) alongside 1 or 2 worker bowlbugs chosen from Egg, Silk, and Nectar types. Individual bowlbugs also appear alongside {{2|Slumbering Beetle}}.

== Bowlbug (Rock) ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Bowlbug (Rock)
|Link   = Slay The Spire 2:Bowlbugs#Bowlbug (Rock)
|Image  = StS2_Bowlbug (Rock).png
|HP     = 45-48
|AscHP  = 46-49
|Powers = {{BD2|Imbalanced}}
|Debut  = Hive
|Type   = Normal
}} 
{{Power Infobox
|Name         = Imbalanced
|Image        = StS2 Icon Imbalanced.png
|Description  = If the enemy's attacks are fully blocked, it becomes {{KW2|Stunned}}.
|Type         = Debuff
|Stacks       = Does not stack
|BetweenTurns = Permanent
|Cap          = 
|GivesToEnemy = Stunned
}}
=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Bowlbug (Rock)}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Headbutt
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (15;{{Asc2|9|16}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Dizzy
|Intent = Stun
|Effect = Stunned. Does nothing.
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Uses {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt}} every turn. However, if {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt}}'s damage is fully prevented by a player, the Bowlbug (Rock) becomes {{KW2|Stunned}} and uses {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Dizzy}} on its next turn, then resumes {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt}}.

=== Notes ===
* The in-game description of {{BD2|Imbalanced}} is somewhat misleading. The Bowlbug (Rock) will become {{KW2|Stunned}} as long as the player has at least 1 {{KW2|Block}} and {{Int|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt|Headbutt's|2}} damage is fully prevented. Some other methods of preventing damage are:
** Playing {{BD2|Buffer}}.
** Reducing the Bowlbug (Rock)'s {{BD2|Strength}}.
** Blocking all but 1 damage and preventing that 1 damage with {{R2|Tungsten Rod}}.
* If the Bowlbug (Rock)'s attack damage is reduced to 0 (such as by {{BD2|Mangle}}) but the player has no {{KW2|Block}}, the Bowlbug (Rock) will ''not'' be {{KW2|Stunned}}.
* If {{KW2|Osty}} takes damage from {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt}}, it will not become {{KW2|Stunned}}.
* Since {{BD2|Imbalanced}} is a debuff, {{C2|Misery}} can apply it to other enemies in the fight.
* In {{2|Multiplayer}}, only one player needs to fully block {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt}} to {{KW2|Stunned|Stun}} the Bowlbug (Rock).

{{Clear}}

== Bowlbug (Egg) ==

|Type   = Normal
|EncounterAliases = Bowlbug (Egg or Nectar), Bowlbug (Lesser)
}}

=== Pattern ===

|Effect = Deals (7;{{Asc2|9|8}}) damage. Gains (7;{{Asc2|9|8}}) {{KW2|Block}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Block
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Uses {{Int2|Bowlbug (Egg)|Bite}} every turn.

{{Clear}}

}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Spin Web
|Intent = Debuff
|Effect = Applies 1 {{BD2|Weak}}.
|GivesToPlayer = Weak
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Alternates between {{Int2|Bowlbug (Silk)|Spin Web}} and {{Int2|Bowlbug (Silk)|Thrash}}.

{{Clear}}

== Bowlbug (Nectar) ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Bowlbug (Nectar)
|Link   = Slay The Spire 2:Bowlbugs#Bowlbug (Nectar)
|Image  = StS2_Bowlbug (Nectar).png
|HP     = 35-38
|AscHP  = 36-39
|Debut  = Hive
|Type   = Normal
|EncounterAliases = Bowlbug (Egg or Nectar), Bowlbug (Lesser)
}}

=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Bowlbug (Nectar)}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Thrash
|Intent = Attack1
|Effect = Deals 3 damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Buff
|Intent = Buff
|Effect = Gains (15;{{Asc2|9|16}}) {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Opens with {{Int2|Bowlbug (Nectar)|Thrash}}, then uses {{Int2|Bowlbug (Nectar)|Buff}} once, then uses {{Int2|Bowlbug (Nectar)|Thrash}} every turn after.

{{Clear}}

pages.name: Fabricator
pages.source_text:
'''Fabricator''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in {{2|Glory}}. It summons bots to fight alongside it.
{{TOC limit|2}}

== Fabricator ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Fabricator
|Image  = StS2_Fabricator.png
|HP     = 150
|AscHP  = 155
|Debut  = Glory
|Type   = Normal
}}
=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Fabricator}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Fabricate
|Intent = Summon
|Effect = Summons 1 defensive bot ({{M2|Guardbot}} or {{M2|Noisebot}}) and 1 aggressive bot ({{M2|Zapbot}} or {{M2|Stabbot}}).
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Fabricating Strike
|Intent = Attack3, Summon
|Effect = Deals (18;{{Asc2|9|21}}) damage. Summons 1 aggressive bot ({{M2|Zapbot}} or {{M2|Stabbot}}).
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Disintegrate
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (11;{{Asc2|9|13}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Each turn, the Fabricator checks if it has fewer than 4 living allies. If so, it randomly uses either {{Int2|Fabricator|Fabricate}} or {{Int2|Fabricator|Fabricating Strike}} (equal weight). If it already has 4 or more allies, it uses {{Int2|Fabricator|Disintegrate}} instead.

The Fabricator avoids summoning the same bot consecutively.

pages.source_text:
'''Gremlin Merc''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in the {{2|Underdocks}}. It starts with {{BD2|Surprise}} and {{BD2|Thievery}}, stealing gold with each attack. When the Gremlin Merc is killed, it summons a {{M2|Fat Gremlin}} and a {{M2|Sneaky Gremlin}}. == Gremlin Merc == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Gremlin Merc |Image = StS2_Gremlin Merc.png |HP = 47-49 |AscHP = 51-53 |Powers = {{BD2|Surprise}}
{{BD2|Thievery}} 20 |Debut = Underdocks |Type = Normal }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Surprise |Image = StS2 Icon Surprise.png |Description = Something is off about this creature... |Type = Buff |Stacks = Does not stack |BetweenTurns = Permanent }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Thievery |Image = StS2 Icon Thievery.png |Description = Steals X Gold when Attacking. |Type = Buff |Stacks = Intensity |BetweenTurns = Permanent |Cap = }} === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Gremlin Merc}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Gimme |Intent = Attack3 |Effect = Deals (7x2;{{Asc2|8|8x2}}) damage. }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Double Smash |Intent = Attack3, Debuff |Effect = Deals (6x2;{{Asc2|8|7x2}}) damage. Applies 2 {{BD2|Weak}}. |GivesToPlayer = Weak }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Hehe |Intent = Attack2, Buff |Effect = Deals (8;{{Asc2|8|9}}) damage. Gains 2 {{BD2|Strength}}. |GivesToEnemy = Strength }} {{Intents Table/end}} Cycles through its moves in a fixed order: # {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Gimme}} # {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Double Smash}} # {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Hehe}} # Back to {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Gimme}} When the Gremlin Merc dies, its {{BD2|Surprise}} power triggers, summoning a {{M2|Fat Gremlin}} and a {{M2|Sneaky Gremlin}}. The Fat Gremlin inherits the stolen gold via {{BD2|Heist}}. === Dialogue === When first using {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Gimme}}.
{{TS|gold|shake|Money!}} {{TS|orange|up|Money!}}
{{Clear}} == Sneaky Gremlin == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Sneaky Gremlin |Link = Slay The Spire 2:Gremlin Merc#Sneaky Gremlin |Image = StS2_Sneaky Gremlin.png |HP = 10-14 |AscHP = 11-15 |Debut = Underdocks |Type = Minion }} The Sneaky Gremlin is a minion summoned when the Gremlin Merc dies. === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Sneaky Gremlin}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Spawned |Intent = Stun |Effect = Wakes up. Does nothing. }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Tackle |Intent = Attack2 |Effect = Deals (9;{{Asc2|9|10}}) damage. }} {{Intents Table/end}} Uses {{Int2|Sneaky Gremlin|Spawned}} on its first turn (does nothing), then uses {{Int2|Sneaky Gremlin|Tackle}} every turn after. {{Clear}} == Fat Gremlin == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Fat Gremlin |Link = Slay The Spire 2:Gremlin Merc#Fat Gremlin |Image = StS2_Fat Gremlin.png |HP = 13-17 |AscHP = 14-18 |Debut = Underdocks |Type = Minion |Powers = {{BD2|Heist}} }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Heist |Image = StS2 Icon Heist.png |Description = When killed, returns all the stolen Gold. |Type = Buff |Stacks = Intensity |BetweenTurns = Permanent |Cap = }} The Fat Gremlin is a minion summoned when the Gremlin Merc dies. It carries any gold the Gremlin Merc stole. === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Fat Gremlin}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Spawned |Intent = Stun |Effect = Wakes up. Does nothing. }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Flee |Intent = Escape |Effect = Flees from combat with any stolen gold. }} {{Intents Table/end}} Uses {{Int2|Fat Gremlin|Spawned}} on its first turn (does nothing), then uses {{Int2|Fat Gremlin|Flee}} every turn after, escaping with the stolen gold. === Dialogue === When using {{Int2|Fat Gremlin|Flee}}.
{{TS|orange|shake|I'm outta here!}}
{{Clear}} == Useful Cards == * Frontloaded damage from cards like {{C2|Assassinate}} can help finish off the '''Gremlin Merc''' before it steals too much of your money. * Recovering {{KW2|Gold}} lost via {{BD2|Thievery}} will trigger {{R2|Dragon Fruit}}. ** The recovered Gold can be bolstered via {{R2|Bowler Hat}}. == Trivia == * The '''Gremlin Merc''' is actually two Gremlins disguised as the {{M|Gremlin Leader}}. * One of the accessories worn by the '''Gremlin Merc''' appears to be a {{R2|Kunai}}. * '''Gremlin Merc''' is the only Enemy in the game whose attack damage increases at {{Asc2|8|Ascension}} instead of {{Asc2|9|Ascension}}. * '''Fat Gremlin''' and '''Sneaky Gremlin''' are the only enemies in Slay the Spire 2 to share a name with enemies from Slay the Spire 1. * '''Fat Gremlin''' is one of only 4 enemies in the game to be incapable of causing damage, the other three being the {{M2|Noisebot}}, {{M2|Guardbot}}, and {{M2|Eye With Teeth}}. == Animations == |-|Gremlin '''Gremlin Merc''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in the {{2|Underdocks}}. It starts with {{BD2|Surprise}} and {{BD2|Thievery}}, stealing gold with each attack. When the Gremlin Merc is killed, it summons a {{M2|Fat Gremlin}} and a {{M2|Sneaky Gremlin}}. == Gremlin Merc == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Gremlin Merc |Image = StS2_Gremlin Merc.png |HP = 47-49 |AscHP = 51-53 |Powers = {{BD2|Surprise}}
{{BD2|Thievery}} 20 |Debut = Underdocks |Type = Normal }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Surprise |Image = StS2 Icon Surprise.png |Description = Something is off about this creature... |Type = Buff |Stacks = Does not stack |BetweenTurns = Permanent }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Thievery |Image = StS2 Icon Thievery.png |Description = Steals X Gold when Attacking. |Type = Buff |Stacks = Intensity |BetweenTurns = Permanent |Cap = }} === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Gremlin Merc}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Gimme |Intent = Attack3 |Effect = Deals (7x2;{{Asc2|8|8x2}}) damage. }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Double Smash |Intent = Attack3, Debuff |Effect = Deals (6x2;{{Asc2|8|7x2}}) damage. Applies 2 {{BD2|Weak}}. |GivesToPlayer = Weak }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Hehe |Intent = Attack2, Buff |Effect = Deals (8;{{Asc2|8|9}}) damage. Gains 2 {{BD2|Strength}}. |GivesToEnemy = Strength }} {{Intents Table/end}} Cycles through its moves in a fixed order: # {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Gimme}} # {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Double Smash}} # {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Hehe}} # Back to {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Gimme}} When the Gremlin Merc dies, its {{BD2|Surprise}} power triggers, summoning a {{M2|Fat Gremlin}} and a {{M2|Sneaky Gremlin}}. The Fat Gremlin inherits the stolen gold via {{BD2|Heist}}. === Dialogue === When first using {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Gimme}}.
{{TS|gold|shake|Money!}} {{TS|orange|up|Money!}}

Does nothing. }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Tackle |Intent = Attack2 |Effect = Deals (9;{{Asc2|9|10}}) damage. }} {{Intents Table/end}} Uses {{Int2|Sneaky Gremlin|Spawned}} on its first turn (does nothing), then uses {{Int2|Sneaky Gremlin|Tackle}} every turn after. {{Clear}} == Fat Gremlin == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Fat Gremlin |Link = Slay The Spire 2:Gremlin Merc#Fat Gremlin |Image = StS2_Fat Gremlin.png |HP = 13-17 |AscHP = 14-18 |Debut = Underdocks |Type = Minion |Powers = {{BD2|Heist}} }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Heist |Image = StS2 Icon Heist.png |Description = When killed, returns all the stolen Gold. |Type = Buff |Stacks = Intensity |BetweenTurns = Permanent |Cap = }} The Fat Gremlin is a minion summoned when the Gremlin Merc dies. It carries any gold the Gremlin Merc stole. === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Fat Gremlin}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Spawned |Intent = Stun |Effect = Wakes up. Does nothing. }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Flee |Intent = Escape |Effect = Flees from combat with any stolen gold. }} {{Intents Table/end}} Uses {{Int2|Fat Gremlin|Spawned}} on its first turn (does nothing), then uses {{Int2|Fat Gremlin|Flee}} every turn after, escaping with the stolen gold. === Dialogue === When using {{Int2|Fat Gremlin|Flee}}.
{{TS|orange|shake|I'm outta here!}}
{{Clear}} == Useful Cards == * Frontloaded damage from cards like {{C2|Assassinate}} can help finish off the '''Gremlin Merc''' before it steals too much of your money. * Recovering {{KW2|Gold}} lost via {{BD2|Thievery}} will trigger {{R2|Dragon Fruit}}. ** The recovered Gold can be bolstered via {{R2|Bowler Hat}}. == Trivia == * The '''Gremlin Merc''' is actually two Gremlins disguised as the {{M|Gremlin Leader}}. * One of the accessories worn by the '''Gremlin Merc''' appears to be a {{R2|Kunai}}. * '''Gremlin Merc''' is the only Enemy in the game whose attack damage increases at {{Asc2|8|Ascension}} instead of {{Asc2|9|Ascension}}. * '''Fat Gremlin''' and '''Sneaky Gremlin''' are the only enemies in Slay the Spire 2 to share a name with enemies from Slay the Spire 1. * '''Fat Gremlin''' is one of only 4 enemies in the game to be incapable of causing damage, the other three being the {{M2|Noisebot}}, {{M2|Guardbot}}, and {{M2|Eye With Teeth}}. == Animations == |-|Gremlin '''Hunter Killer''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in {{2|Hive}}.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Hunter Killer}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Tenderizing Goop
|Intent = Debuff

|GivesToPlayer = Tender
}}
{{Intents Table/row

|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (17;{{Asc2|9|19}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Puncture
|Intent = Attack4
|Effect = Deals (7;{{Asc2|9|8}}) damage ×3.
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Always opens with {{Int2|Hunter Killer|Tenderizing Goop}}. After that, randomly uses {{Int2|Hunter Killer|Bite}} or {{Int2|Hunter Killer|Puncture}}, with {{Int2|Hunter Killer|Puncture}} being twice as likely. {{Int2|Hunter Killer|Bite}} cannot be used twice in a row.

== Notes ==
* The {{BD2|Tender}} debuff reduces {{BD2|Strength}} and {{BD2|Dexterity}} after all of a played card's effects are resolved, so that the damage and {{KW2|Block}} values displayed on cards are accurate.
* Whenever a card's effect plays another card(s) as part of its resolution (such as {{C2|Cascade}} or {{C2|Catastrophe}}) or when a {{KW2|Sly}} card is discarded by a card's effect, that initial card does not resolve until the card(s) it plays have resolved. Thus, {{BD2|Tender}} does not reduce {{BD2|Strength}} and {{BD2|Dexterity}} for that card play until after the other cards are played.
** The player still loses {{BD2|Strength}} and {{BD2|Dexterity}} equal to the total number of cards played in the combo.
** For instance, when playing {{C2|Knife Trap}} to play 2 {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted|2}} {{C2|Shiv|Shivs}}, {{BD2|Tender}} does not reduce {{BD2|Strength}} and {{BD2|Dexterity}} for {{C2|Knife Trap}} itself until all the played {{C2|Shiv|Shivs}} are played (at which point {{C2|Knife Trap}} resolves). The first {{C2|Shiv}} will deal full damage and trigger {{BD2|Tender}}, and then the second {{C2|Shiv}} will deal 1 less damage and trigger {{BD2|Tender}} again. Afterwards, {{C2|Knife Trap}} resolves and triggers {{BD2|Tender}} for a third time.

'''Infested Prism''' is an {{2|Elites|Elite}} {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in {{2|Hive}}. 

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Infested Prism}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Jab
|Intent = Attack4
|Effect = Deals (15;{{Asc2|9|17}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Radiate
|Intent = Attack3, Defend
|Effect = Deals (11;{{Asc2|9|13}}) damage. Gains (16;{{Asc2|9|18}}) {{KW2|Block}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Block
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Whirlwind
|Intent = Attack4
|Effect = Deals (5;{{Asc2|9|6}}) damage ×3.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Pulsate
|Intent = Attack3, Buff, Defend
|Effect = Deal (8;{{Asc2|9|10}}) damage. Gains (20;{{Asc2|8|22}}) {{KW2|Block}} and {{BD2|Vital Spark}} (2;{{Asc2|9|3}}).
|GivesToEnemy = Block, Vital Spark
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
The Infested Prism repeats a fixed four-move cycle:
# {{Int2|Infested Prism|Jab}}
# {{Int2|Infested Prism|Radiate}}
# {{Int2|Infested Prism|Whirlwind}}
# {{Int2|Infested Prism|Pulsate}}

== Useful Cards ==
* Cards which are not Skills but still provide {{KW2|Block}}, such as {{C2|Iron Wave}} or {{C2|Afterimage}}, can prevent damage without gaining {{BD2|Tainted}}.
* Expensive skills like {{C2|Reanimate}} or {{C2|Impervious}}, which provide significant benefits while only gaining {{KW2|Tainted}} once, tend to be more effective than cheaper skills like {{C2|Deflect}} or {{C2|Prepared}}.
* Decks which rely on skills like {{C2|Deadly Poison}} or {{C2|No Escape}} to kill enemies are generally not effective against this enemy, as it will be difficult to deal damage to the '''Infested Prism''' without taking additional damage yourself.

== Trivia ==
* Many players often refer to the '''Infested Prism''' as "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doritos Dorito]" due to its shape and color.

{{Sequel Disambiguation}}
'''Slimes''' are normal {{2|Monsters|Enemies}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}. They come in four varieties: two Leaf Slimes and two Twig Slimes, each in a small (S) and medium (M) size. They appear together in the Slimes encounter and as companions in other Overgrowth encounters.
== Encounters ==
* Easy Slimes: 1 of each (S) Slime, and a Random (M) Slime.
* Hard Slimes: 1 of each Slime variety.
* {{M2|Flyconid}} and a Random (M) Slime.
* {{M2|Slithering Strangler}} and 1 of each (S) Slime.

{{Sequel Disambiguation}}
'''Slimes''' are normal {{2|Monsters|Enemies}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}. They come in four varieties: two Leaf Slimes and two Twig Slimes, each in a small (S) and medium (M) size. They appear together in the Slimes encounter and as companions in other Overgrowth encounters.
== Encounters ==
* Easy Slimes: 1 of each (S) Slime, and a Random (M) Slime.
* Hard Slimes: 1 of each Slime variety.
* {{M2|Flyconid}} and a Random (M) Slime.
* {{M2|Slithering Strangler}} and 1 of each (S) Slime.
* {{M2|Slithering Strangler}} and a Random (M) Slime.

}}

* Uses {{Int2|Living Shield|Shield Slam}} every turn while the '''Turret Operator''' is alive.
** Once the '''Turret Operator''' is killed, switches to {{Int2|Living Shield|Smash}} every turn.

{{Clear}}

== Useful Cards ==
* The '''Turret Operator''''s damage is split into multiple hits with low damage on each, so {{BD2|Strength}} reduction from cards like {{C2|Piercing Wail}}, {{C2|Shared Fate}} or {{C2|Mangle}} will decrease his damage significantly and will often set it to 0.
* The '''Turret Operator''' will take five times as much damage as most enemies from {{BD2|Thorns}}.

== Trivia ==
* '''Turret Operator and Living Shield''' appear to be designed in reference to Slay the Spire 1's {{M|Centurion}} and {{M|Mystic}}. The two fights' combatants share similar proportions, and both '''Living Shield''' and Centurion employ an additional attack if their smaller companion is killed.

{{Event Infobox |Name=The Lantern Key |Image=StS2_Mysterious Knight.png }} {{Small Card Infobox|Lantern Key|2}} {{E2|The Lantern Key}} is an {{2|Event}} found exclusively in the {{2|Hive}}. It is a combat event. The {{C2|Lantern Key}} can be used in the {{E2|War Historian, Repy}} event in Act 3. == Options == {{Frame|Return the Key}} {{TS|positive||Gain 100 Gold.}}
{{Frame|Keep the Key}} Enter combat against a {{2|Mysterious Knight}} for the {{C2|Lantern Key}} card. == Dialogue ==
You come upon a faintly glowing key and go to pick it up. "Been looking all over for that key! Now if you don't mind..." This person looks like bad news but maybe it's not good to be judgy.
{{Frame|Return the Key}}
The stranger thanks you for your help, and rewards you handsomely.
{{Frame|Keep the Key}}
The stranger looks at you menacingly. It seems like only one of you is making it out of here with the key.
== Notes == * If you choose to {{Frame|Keep the Key}}, the {{2|Mysterious Knight}} combat counts as a normal combat encounter for purposes such as {{R2|Prayer Wheel}} and will drop normal combat rewards along with the {{C2|Lantern Key}}. == Mysterious Knight == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Mysterious Knight |Image = StS2_Mysterious Knight.png |HP = 101 |AscHP = 108 |Powers = {{BD2|Strength}} 6
{{BD2|Plating}} 6 |Debut = Hive |Type = Normal }} '''Mysterious Knight''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} encountered in the {{E2|The Lantern Key}} event. It is a stronger version of the {{M2|Flail Knight}} with innate {{BD2|Strength}} and {{BD2|Plating}}. === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Mysterious Knight}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Breaker |Intent = Buff |Effect = Gains 3 {{BD2|Strength}}. |GivesToEnemy = Strength }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Flail |Intent = Attack3 |Effect = Deals (9;{{Asc2|9|10}}) damage x2. }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Ram |Intent = Attack3 |Effect = Deals (15;{{Asc2|9|17}}) damage. }} {{Intents Table/end}} Opens with {{Int2|Mysterious Knight|Ram}}, then randomly picks {{Int2|Mysterious Knight|Breaker}} (equal chance), {{Int2|Mysterious Knight|Flail}} (double chance), or {{Int2|Mysterious Knight|Ram}} (double chance). '''Nibbit''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Nibbit}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Butt
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (12;{{Asc2|9|13}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Hesitant Slice
|Intent = Attack2, Defend
|Effect = Deals (6;{{Asc2|9|7}}) damage. Gains (5;{{Asc2|8|6}}) {{KW2|Block}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Block
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Hiss
|Intent = Buff
|Effect = Gains (2;{{Asc2|9|3}}) {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}

Intent cycles in order. After {{Int2|Nibbit|Hiss}} their intent wraps back around to {{Int2|Nibbit|Butt}}, followed by {{Int2|Nibbit|Hesitant Slice}} and then {{Int2|Nibbit|Hiss}} again. Starting intent is encounter dependent.

==== Solo Encounter ====

When alone (Nibbits Weak encounter), the Nibbit opens with {{Int2|Nibbit|Butt}}. It's good strategy to aim to win on one of the {{Int2|Nibbit|Butt}} repeats, so either turn 4 or 7. Nibbit buffs the turn prior, giving you 2 full turns to spend energy on nothing but attacks and finish the combat before the big attack lands.

pages.name: Ovicopter
pages.source_text:
'''Ovicopter''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in the {{2|Hive}}. It summons {{M2|Tough Egg|Tough Eggs}} that hatch into {{M2|Hatchling|Hatchlings}}.

== Ovicopter ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Ovicopter
|Image  = StS2_Ovicopter.png
|HP     = 124-130
|AscHP  = 126-132
|Debut  = Hive
|Type   = Normal
}}
=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Ovicopter}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Lay Eggs
|Intent = Summon
|Effect = Summons 3 {{2|Tough Egg|Tough Eggs}}.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Smash
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (16;{{Asc2|9|17}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Tenderizer
|Intent = Attack2, Debuff
|Effect = Deals (7;{{Asc2|9|8}}) damage. Applies 2 {{BD2|Vulnerable}}.
|GivesToPlayer = Vulnerable
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Nutritional Paste
|Intent = Buff
|Effect = Gains (3;{{Asc2|9|4}}) {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Always opens with {{Int2|Ovicopter|Lay Eggs}} to summon 3 {{2|Tough Egg|Tough Eggs}}, then uses {{Int2|Ovicopter|Smash}}, then {{Int2|Ovicopter|Tenderizer}}.

After {{Int2|Ovicopter|Tenderizer}}, it checks how many allies it has. If it has 3 or fewer living allies, it uses {{Int2|Ovicopter|Lay Eggs}} again. If it has more than 3, it uses {{Int2|Ovicopter|Nutritional Paste}} instead. Then the cycle continues with {{Int2|Ovicopter|Smash}} and {{Int2|Ovicopter|Tenderizer}}.

{{Clear}}

== Tough Egg ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Tough Egg
|Link   = Slay the Spire 2:Ovicopter#Tough Egg
|Image  = StS2_Tough Egg.png
|HP     = 14-18
|AscHP  = 15-19
|Powers = {{BD2|Minion}} {{BD2|Hatch}} 2
|Type   = Minion
|Debut  = Hive
|EncounterAliases = Tough Egg (+)
}} 
{{Power Infobox|Minion|2}}
{{Power Infobox
|Name         = Hatch
|Image        = StS2 Icon Hatch.png
|Description  = Hatches after X turns.
|Type         = Buff
|Stacks       = Duration
|BetweenTurns = Decremented
|Cap          = 
}}
The Tough Egg is a minion summoned by Ovicopter via {{Int2|Ovicopter|Lay Eggs}}. It starts with the {{BD2|Hatch}} power, which counts down over turns.

=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Tough Egg}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Hatch
|Intent = Summon
|Effect = Hatches into a Hatchling. Removes all powers except {{BD2|Minion}}.
|PowerGives = Minion
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
The Tough Egg waits while its {{BD2|Hatch}} timer counts down. When the timer expires, it uses {{Int2|Tough Egg|Hatch}} to transform into a {{M2|Hatchling}} with new HP.

{{Clear}}

== Hatchling ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Hatchling
|Link   = Slay the Spire 2:Ovicopter#Hatchling
|Image  = StS2_Hatchling.png
|HP     = 19-22
|AscHP  = 20-23
|Powers = {{BD2|Minion}}
|Type   = Minion
|Debut  = Hive
|EncounterAliases = Tough Egg (+)
}}
{{Power Infobox|Minion|2}}
The Hatchling is a minion that spawns from a {{M2|Tough Egg}}

=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Hatchling}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Nibble
|Intent = Attack1
|Effect = Deals (4;{{Asc2|9|5}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Uses {{Int2|Hatchling|Nibble}} every turn.

{{Clear}}

== Notes ==
* {{BD2|Hatch}} timer starts at 2 if summoned during the enemy turn, or 1 during the player turn.
* Hatching removes all negative status effects which were applied to the '''Tough Egg'''.

{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Phrog Parasite
|Image  = StS2_Phrog Parasite.png

|Debut  = Overgrowth
|Type   = Elite

'''Phrog Parasite''' is an {{2|Elites|Elite}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Phrog Parasite}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Infect
|Intent = StatusCard
|Effect = Shuffles 3 {{C2|Infection}} into your discard pile.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Lash
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (4;{{Asc2|9|5}}) damage ×4.
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Phrog Parasite alternates between its two moves:
# {{Int2|Phrog Parasite|Infect}}
# {{Int2|Phrog Parasite|Lash}}
# Back to {{Int2|Phrog Parasite|Infect}}, and so on.

When Phrog Parasite dies, {{BD2|Infested}} triggers and 4 {{M|Wriggler|Wrigglers|2}} are summoned. They will be {{KW2|Stunned}} and do nothing on their first turn. The fight continues until all Wrigglers are defeated.

== Notes ==
* Whether the Wrigglers are {{KW2|Stunned}} on the player's next turn depends on if the Phrog Parasite dies during the player turn or the enemy turn:
** If the Phrog Parasite is killed with an Attack card or damage from an Orb, the Wrigglers will be {{KW2|Stunned}} during this turn, ''not'' the player's next turn.
** If the Phrog Parasite dies to {{BD2|Poison}} or {{BD2|Doom}}, then the Wrigglers will have no {{2|Intent}} when spawned. They will be {{KW2|Stunned}} during the player's next turn.
*** This also applies if the Phrog Parasite dies as a result of its own attack, such as by {{BD2|Thorns}} or {{C2|Necro Mastery}}.
<!--
Confirm this is all correct, I've tested but may have missed something or made a mistake
-->
* '''Infections''' deal damage during the player turn, so the damage will activate cards like {{C2|Inferno}} or {{C2|Rupture}}.
* {{C2|Omnislice}} damages the target, then damages all other enemies afterwards. If the first hit kills the '''Phrog Parasite''', then it will spawn '''Wrigglers''' before the card resolves and the Wrigglers will also take damage.

== Useful Cards ==
* Frontloaded damage cards like {{C2|Perfected Strike}}, {{C2|Backstab}}, and {{C2|Defile}} can be useful for taking down the Phrog Parasite before it can create too many Infections. They can also finish off individual Wrigglers quickly.
* {{C2|Deathbringer}}, {{C2|Deadly Poison}}, and other cards which apply {{BD2|Poison}} or {{BD2|Doom}} can gain an extra turn before the Wrigglers attack, if the Phrog Parasite dies to their damage.
* Attacks which target all enemies like {{C2|Dagger Spray}}, {{C2|Bone Shards}}, and {{C2|Whirlwind}} can damage all of the Wrigglers at once.
* {{C2|Inferno}} deals consistent damage to all enemies every turn. It also triggers whenever '''Infections''' deal unblocked damage.
* Cards which can discard, {{KW2|Exhaust}}, or {{KW2|Transform}} '''Infections''', such as {{C2|Burning Pact}} or {{C2|Hidden Daggers}}, can prevent them from dealing damage.
** {{C2|Compact}} and {{C2|Flak Cannon}} are especially noteworthy, since they remove all '''Infections''' in Hand or in all zones, respectively.

== Wriggler ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Wriggler
|Link   = Slay the Spire 2:Phrog Parasite#Wriggler
|Image  = StS2_Wriggler.png
|HP     = 17-21
|AscHP  = 18-22
|Debut  = Overgrowth
|Type   = Normal
}}
'''Wriggler''' is a normal {{2|Enemy}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}. It appears in the {{E2|Dense Vegetation}} event and is also summoned by {{M2|Phrog Parasite}} upon its death.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Wriggler}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Nasty Bite
|Intent = Attack2
|Effect = Deals (6;{{Asc2|9|7}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Wriggle
|Intent = Buff, StatusCard
|Effect = Shuffles 1 {{C2|Infection}} into your discard pile. Gains 2 {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Wrigglers alternate between {{Int2|Wriggler|Nasty Bite}} and {{Int2|Wriggler|Wriggle}}. When multiple Wrigglers are present, they start offset from each other: odd-numbered Wrigglers begin with {{Int2|Wriggler|Nasty Bite}} and even-numbered Wrigglers begin with {{Int2|Wriggler|Wriggle}}.

When summoned by {{M2|Phrog Parasite}} (via {{BD2|Infested}}), each Wriggler spends its first turn {{KW2|Stunned}} before beginning its pattern. In the {{E2|Dense Vegetation}} event, 4 Wrigglers appear at once, starting their patterns immediately (not {{KW2|Stunned}}).

{{Clear}}
== Trivia ==
* The {{R2|Paper Phrog}} is likely based on the same type of creature being {{BD2|Infested}} by the Phrog Parasite.

'''Scroll of Biting''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in {{2|Glory}}. It appears in groups of 3 (weak) or 4 (normal), each starting on a different move.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Scroll of Biting}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Chomp
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (14;{{Asc2|9|16}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = More Teeth
|Intent = Buff
|Effect = Gains 2 {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Chew
|Intent = Attack2
|Effect = Deals (5;{{Asc2|9|6}}) damage 2 times.
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Each Scroll of Biting starts on a different move in the cycle. The pattern is: {{Int2|Scroll of Biting|Chomp}}, then {{Int2|Scroll of Biting|More Teeth}}, then {{Int2|Scroll of Biting|Chew}}.

After {{Int2|Scroll of Biting|Chew}}, it randomly picks either {{Int2|Scroll of Biting|Chomp}} (cannot repeat) or {{Int2|Scroll of Biting|Chew}} (weight 2), then continues the cycle from that point.

== Notes ==
* If the Scroll of Biting deals unblocked damage to {{KW2|Osty}}, neither he nor the player loses any max HP from {{BD2|Paper Cuts}}.
* If {{R2|Tungsten Rod}} reduces the unblocked damage taken from 1 to 0 (for example, if a '''Scroll of Biting''' deals 14 damage to a player with 13 {{KW2|Block}}) then the player will not lose max HP.
* If the Scroll of Biting dies from reflected damage such as {{BD2|Thorns}} or {{BD2|Flame Barrier}} while dealing unblocked damage to the player, the player will not lose any max HP from {{BD2|Paper Cuts}}.

== Pattern ==

}}

The Skulking Colony repeats the same four moves in order:
# {{Int2|Skulking Colony|Zoom}}
# {{Int2|Skulking Colony|Zoom}}
# {{Int2|Skulking Colony|Inertia}}
# {{Int2|Skulking Colony|Piercing Stabs}}

== Notes ==
* {{BD2|Hardened Shell}} resets on both the start of the ''player's turn'' as well as the start of the ''Skulking Colony's turn.'' Since {{BD2|Poison}} deals damage at the start of an enemy's turn, it is possible to deal a maximum of 40 damage in a single turn by doing 20 attack damage and having 20 stacks of {{BD2|Poison}} on it at the same time.
* {{BD2|Thorns}}, {{BD2|Reflect}}, {{BD2|Flame Barrier}}, {{BD2|Necro Mastery}}, and {{BD2|Demise}} also trigger on the enemy turn.
* {{BD2|Hardened Shell}} can be partially bypassed by {{R2|The Boot}}. If the enemy can only lose 1 to 4 more HP this turn, hitting it with an Attack will cause it to take 5 damage instead of the limited amount.
** Any further Attacks this turn will still deal 0 damage and will not be affected.

== Trivia ==
* Skulking Colony is male.<ref> "Additionally I found that the Dazed statuses actually worked against the design goals of his power" https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2868840/view/507357499795439629?l=english</ref>

pages.name: Sneaky Gremlin
pages.source_text:
'''Gremlin Merc''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in the {{2|Underdocks}}. It starts with {{BD2|Surprise}} and {{BD2|Thievery}}, stealing gold with each attack. When the Gremlin Merc is killed, it summons a {{M2|Fat Gremlin}} and a {{M2|Sneaky Gremlin}}. == Gremlin Merc == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Gremlin Merc |Image = StS2_Gremlin Merc.png |HP = 47-49 |AscHP = 51-53 |Powers = {{BD2|Surprise}}
{{BD2|Thievery}} 20 |Debut = Underdocks |Type = Normal }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Surprise |Image = StS2 Icon Surprise.png |Description = Something is off about this creature... |Type = Buff |Stacks = Does not stack |BetweenTurns = Permanent }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Thievery |Image = StS2 Icon Thievery.png |Description = Steals X Gold when Attacking. |Type = Buff |Stacks = Intensity |BetweenTurns = Permanent |Cap = }} === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Gremlin Merc}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Gimme |Intent = Attack3 |Effect = Deals (7x2;{{Asc2|8|8x2}}) damage. }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Double Smash |Intent = Attack3, Debuff |Effect = Deals (6x2;{{Asc2|8|7x2}}) damage. Applies 2 {{BD2|Weak}}. |GivesToPlayer = Weak }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Hehe |Intent = Attack2, Buff |Effect = Deals (8;{{Asc2|8|9}}) damage. Gains 2 {{BD2|Strength}}. |GivesToEnemy = Strength }} {{Intents Table/end}} Cycles through its moves in a fixed order: # {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Gimme}} # {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Double Smash}} # {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Hehe}} # Back to {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Gimme}} When the Gremlin Merc dies, its {{BD2|Surprise}} power triggers, summoning a {{M2|Fat Gremlin}} and a {{M2|Sneaky Gremlin}}. The Fat Gremlin inherits the stolen gold via {{BD2|Heist}}. === Dialogue === When first using {{Int2|Gremlin Merc|Gimme}}.
{{TS|gold|shake|Money!}} {{TS|orange|up|Money!}}
{{Clear}} == Sneaky Gremlin == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Sneaky Gremlin |Link = Slay The Spire 2:Gremlin Merc#Sneaky Gremlin |Image = StS2_Sneaky Gremlin.png |HP = 10-14 |AscHP = 11-15 |Debut = Underdocks |Type = Minion }} The Sneaky Gremlin is a minion summoned when the Gremlin Merc dies. === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Sneaky Gremlin}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Spawned |Intent = Stun |Effect = Wakes up. Does nothing. }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Tackle |Intent = Attack2 |Effect = Deals (9;{{Asc2|9|10}}) damage. }} {{Intents Table/end}} Uses {{Int2|Sneaky Gremlin|Spawned}} on its first turn (does nothing), then uses {{Int2|Sneaky Gremlin|Tackle}} every turn after. {{Clear}} == Fat Gremlin == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Fat Gremlin |Link = Slay The Spire 2:Gremlin Merc#Fat Gremlin |Image = StS2_Fat Gremlin.png |HP = 13-17 |AscHP = 14-18 |Debut = Underdocks |Type = Minion |Powers = {{BD2|Heist}} }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Heist |Image = StS2 Icon Heist.png |Description = When killed, returns all the stolen Gold. |Type = Buff |Stacks = Intensity |BetweenTurns = Permanent |Cap = }} The Fat Gremlin is a minion summoned when the Gremlin Merc dies. It carries any gold the Gremlin Merc stole. === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Fat Gremlin}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Spawned |Intent = Stun |Effect = Wakes up. Does nothing. }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Flee |Intent = Escape |Effect = Flees from combat with any stolen gold. }} {{Intents Table/end}} Uses {{Int2|Fat Gremlin|Spawned}} on its first turn (does nothing), then uses {{Int2|Fat Gremlin|Flee}} every turn after, escaping with the stolen gold. === Dialogue === When using {{Int2|Fat Gremlin|Flee}}.
{{TS|orange|shake|I'm outta here!}}
{{Clear}} == Useful Cards == * Frontloaded damage from cards like {{C2|Assassinate}} can help finish off the '''Gremlin Merc''' before it steals too much of your money. * Recovering {{KW2|Gold}} lost via {{BD2|Thievery}} will trigger {{R2|Dragon Fruit}}. ** The recovered Gold can be bolstered via {{R2|Bowler Hat}}. == Trivia == * The '''Gremlin Merc''' is actually two Gremlins disguised as the {{M|Gremlin Leader}}. * One of the accessories worn by the '''Gremlin Merc''' appears to be a {{R2|Kunai}}. * '''Gremlin Merc''' is the only Enemy in the game whose attack damage increases at {{Asc2|8|Ascension}} instead of {{Asc2|9|Ascension}}. * '''Fat Gremlin''' and '''Sneaky Gremlin''' are the only enemies in Slay the Spire 2 to share a name with enemies from Slay the Spire 1. * '''Fat Gremlin''' is one of only 4 enemies in the game to be incapable of causing damage, the other three being the {{M2|Noisebot}}, {{M2|Guardbot}}, and {{M2|Eye With Teeth}}. == Animations == |-|Gremlin '''Terror Eel''' is an {{2|Elites|Elite}} {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in the {{2|Underdocks}}.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Terror Eel}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Crash
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (16;{{Asc2|9|18}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Thrash
|Intent = Attack2, Buff
|Effect = Deals (3x3;{{Asc2|9|4x3}}) damage. Gains 6 {{BD2|Vigor}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Vigor
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Stun
|Intent = Stun
|Effect = Stunned. Does nothing.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Terror
|Intent = Debuff
|Effect = Applies 99 {{BD2|Vulnerable}}.
|GivesToPlayer = Vulnerable
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
The Terror Eel alternates between {{Int2|Terror Eel|Crash}} and {{Int2|Terror Eel|Thrash}}, starting with {{Int2|Terror Eel|Crash}}. Because {{Int2|Terror Eel|Thrash}} gives the Terror Eel 6 {{BD2|Vigor}}, {{Int2|Terror Eel|Crash}} always deals 22({{Asc2|9|24}}) damage from turn 3 onwards.

When its HP drops to its {{BD2|Shriek}} threshold (70, or {{Asc2|8|75}}), it becomes {{KW2|Stunned}} and then uses {{Int2|Terror Eel|Terror}} before resuming the Crash/Thrash cycle.

* {{Int2|Terror Eel|Terror}} applies 99 {{BD2|Vulnerable}}, which effectively makes the player take 50% more damage from attacks for the rest of the fight.

== Trivia ==
* Terror Eel's name and {{Int2|Terror Eel|Terror}} skill are a reference to the card {{C|Terror||1}} from Slay the Spire.

{{E2|The Merchant???}} is an {{2|Event}} found in the {{2|Hive}} and the {{2|Glory}}. At first glance, it appears to be a normal {{2|Merchant}} encounter, but the shop sells a set of knock-off {{2|Relics}}.

== Conditions ==
* Cannot appear in {{2|Multiplayer}}.
* Only appears in {{2|Acts}} 2 and 3.
* Only appears if the player has at least 100 {{KW2|Gold}} or if one of the currently held potions is {{P2|Foul Potion}}.

== Relics ==
The fake Merchant's shop only contains a set of 6 Relics, each costing a random amount between 43-57 {{2|Gold}}. The 6 Relics are randomly chosen out of the list below:

* {{R2|Anchor???}}
* {{R2|Blood Vial???}}
* {{R2|Happy Flower???}}
* {{R2|Lee's Waffle???}}
* {{R2|Mango???}}
* {{R2|Orichalcum???}}
* {{R2|Snecko Eye???}}
* {{R2|Strike Dummy???}}
* {{R2|Venerable Tea Set???}}

== Combat ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = The Merchant???
|Image  = StS2_The Merchant???.png
|HP     = 165
|AscHP  = 175
|Debut  = Hive
|Type   = Normal
}}
If a {{P2|Foul Potion}} is owned, it can be thrown at the fake Merchant to trigger combat. Winning the combat will give 300 Gold, the ability to take the Relics that were for sale, and {{R2|The Merchant's Rug???}}, which does nothing. The relics can be skipped if they are not wanted.

== Pattern ==

|Effect = Deals (9;{{Asc2|9|10}}) damage. Applies 1 {{BD2|Frail}}.
|GivesToPlayer = Frail
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Enrage
|Intent = Buff
|Effect = Gains 2 {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
* Always uses {{Int2|The Merchant???|Swipe}} first. 
* {{Int2|The Merchant???|Swipe}}, {{Int2|The Merchant???|Spew Coins}}, and {{Int2|The Merchant???|Enrage}} randomly lead into 1 of the 3 other possible moves 
** Cannot use the same move twice in a row.
* {{Int2|The Merchant???|Enrage}} can only be chosen once every 3 turns. 
* {{Int2|The Merchant???|Throw Relic}} is randomly followed up by {{Int2|The Merchant???|Swipe}} or {{Int2|The Merchant???|Spew Coins}}.

'''Thieving Hopper''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in {{2|Hive}}.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Thieving Hopper}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Thievery
|Intent = Attack3, CardDebuff
|Effect = Deals (17;{{Asc2|9|19}}) damage. {{BD2|Swipe}} a card from your deck.
|GivesToEnemy = Swipe
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Flutter
|Intent = Buff
|Effect = Gains {{BD2|Flutter}} (takes 50% less Attack damage, must be hit 5 times to {{KW2|Stunned|Stun}} it).
|GivesToEnemy = Flutter
|PowerGives = Stunned
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Hat Trick
|Intent = Attack4
|Effect = Deals (21;{{Asc2|9|23}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Nab
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (14;{{Asc2|9|16}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Escape
|Intent = Escape
|Effect = Flees the combat, taking any stolen cards with it.
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
The Thieving Hopper follows a fixed sequence:
* {{Int2|Thieving Hopper|Thievery}} (stealing a card and dealing damage)
* {{Int2|Thieving Hopper|Flutter}} (gaining damage reduction)
* {{Int2|Thieving Hopper|Hat Trick}}
* {{Int2|Thieving Hopper|Nab}}
* {{Int2|Thieving Hopper|Escape}} (fleeing the fight permanently)

If it escapes, any cards it stole are lost for the rest of the run. Killing it before it escapes returns the stolen cards.

== Notes ==
* If the enemy escapes, the player does not receive any gold, but still gets a card reward and a possible potion drop.

* The card stolen by Swipe follows a set order of priority:

1. Non-{{KW2|Imbued}} {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} cards

2. Non-{{KW2|Imbued}} {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}}, {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Common|Common}}, and {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Event|Event}} cards

3. Non-{{KW2|Imbued}} {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Basic|Basic}} and {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Quest|Quest}} cards

4. {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Ancient|Ancient}} cards or cards that are {{KW2|Imbued}}

5. {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Curse|Curse}} cards

* Only cards currently in the player's draw or discard pile when the move is used will be selected. This means under the right circumstances the move can be utilized to remove {{KW2|Eternal}} cards from the player's deck.
* The returned card can be skipped, which means it is possible to defeat the Thieving Hopper, receive all the usual combat rewards and still have a card removed if it is so desired.
* When choosing to take back the stolen card, all the usual interactions on adding a card to the deck apply (e.g. {{R2|Bing Bong}}, or {{R2|Lucky Fysh}}).
* {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Token|Token}} cards and {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Status|Status}} cards can never be stolen as this would result in being able to add a temporary card into your deck permanently. This also applies to other temporary cards, such as those created by potions.

pages.source_text:
'''Ovicopter''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in the {{2|Hive}}. It summons {{M2|Tough Egg|Tough Eggs}} that hatch into {{M2|Hatchling|Hatchlings}}.

== Ovicopter ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Ovicopter
|Image  = StS2_Ovicopter.png
|HP     = 124-130
|AscHP  = 126-132
|Debut  = Hive
|Type   = Normal
}}
=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Ovicopter}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Lay Eggs
|Intent = Summon
|Effect = Summons 3 {{2|Tough Egg|Tough Eggs}}.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Smash
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (16;{{Asc2|9|17}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Tenderizer
|Intent = Attack2, Debuff
|Effect = Deals (7;{{Asc2|9|8}}) damage. Applies 2 {{BD2|Vulnerable}}.
|GivesToPlayer = Vulnerable
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Nutritional Paste
|Intent = Buff
|Effect = Gains (3;{{Asc2|9|4}}) {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Always opens with {{Int2|Ovicopter|Lay Eggs}} to summon 3 {{2|Tough Egg|Tough Eggs}}, then uses {{Int2|Ovicopter|Smash}}, then {{Int2|Ovicopter|Tenderizer}}.

After {{Int2|Ovicopter|Tenderizer}}, it checks how many allies it has. If it has 3 or fewer living allies, it uses {{Int2|Ovicopter|Lay Eggs}} again. If it has more than 3, it uses {{Int2|Ovicopter|Nutritional Paste}} instead. Then the cycle continues with {{Int2|Ovicopter|Smash}} and {{Int2|Ovicopter|Tenderizer}}.

{{Clear}}

== Tough Egg ==
{{Enemy Infobox

|Link   = Slay the Spire 2:Ovicopter#Tough Egg

|EncounterAliases = Tough Egg (+)
}} 
{{Power Infobox|Minion|2}}
{{Power Infobox

|Image        = StS2 Icon Hatch.png
|Description  = Hatches after X turns.
|Type         = Buff
|Stacks       = Duration
|BetweenTurns = Decremented
|Cap          = 
}}
The Tough Egg is a minion summoned by Ovicopter via {{Int2|Ovicopter|Lay Eggs}}. It starts with the {{BD2|Hatch}} power, which counts down over turns.

=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Tough Egg}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Hatch
|Intent = Summon
|Effect = Hatches into a Hatchling. Removes all powers except {{BD2|Minion}}.
|PowerGives = Minion
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
The Tough Egg waits while its {{BD2|Hatch}} timer counts down. When the timer expires, it uses {{Int2|Tough Egg|Hatch}} to transform into a {{M2|Hatchling}} with new HP.

{{Clear}}

== Hatchling ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Hatchling
|Link   = Slay the Spire 2:Ovicopter#Hatchling
|Image  = StS2_Hatchling.png
|HP     = 19-22
|AscHP  = 20-23
|Powers = {{BD2|Minion}}
|Type   = Minion
|Debut  = Hive
|EncounterAliases = Tough Egg (+)
}}
{{Power Infobox|Minion|2}}
The Hatchling is a minion that spawns from a {{M2|Tough Egg}}

=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Hatchling}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Nibble
|Intent = Attack1
|Effect = Deals (4;{{Asc2|9|5}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Uses {{Int2|Hatchling|Nibble}} every turn.

{{Clear}}

== Notes ==
* {{BD2|Hatch}} timer starts at 2 if summoned during the enemy turn, or 1 during the player turn.
* Hatching removes all negative status effects which were applied to the '''Tough Egg'''.

'''Turret Operator''' is a weak {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} encounter found in {{2|Glory}}, featuring a Living Shield and a Turret Operator.

== Turret Operator ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Turret Operator
|Image  = StS2_Turret Operator.png
|HP     = 41

|Debut  = Glory
|Type   = Normal
}}

|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (3;{{Asc2|9|4}}) damage x5.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Loading
|Intent = Buff
|Effect = Gains 1 {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Follows a fixed 3-move cycle:
# {{Int2|Turret Operator|Unload!}}
# {{Int2|Turret Operator|Unload!}}
# {{Int2|Turret Operator|Loading}}

{{Clear}}

== Living Shield ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Living Shield
|Image  = StS2_Living Shield.png
|HP     = 55
|AscHP  = 65
|Powers = {{BD2|Rampart}} 25
|Debut  = Glory
|Type   = Normal
}} 
{{Power Infobox
|Name         = Rampart
|Image        = StS2 Icon Rampart.png
|Description  = At the start of the player's turn, Turret Operator gains X {{KW2|Block}}.
|Type         = Buff
|Stacks       = Intensity
|BetweenTurns = Permanent
|Cap          = 
|GivesToEnemy = Block
}}
=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Living Shield}}
{{Intents Table/row

|Intent = Attack1
|Effect = Deals 6 damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Smash
|Intent = Attack3, Buff
|Effect = Deals (16;{{Asc2|9|18}}) damage. Gains 3 {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
* Uses {{Int2|Living Shield|Shield Slam}} every turn while the '''Turret Operator''' is alive.
** Once the '''Turret Operator''' is killed, switches to {{Int2|Living Shield|Smash}} every turn.

{{Clear}}

== Useful Cards ==
* The '''Turret Operator''''s damage is split into multiple hits with low damage on each, so {{BD2|Strength}} reduction from cards like {{C2|Piercing Wail}}, {{C2|Shared Fate}} or {{C2|Mangle}} will decrease his damage significantly and will often set it to 0.
* The '''Turret Operator''' will take five times as much damage as most enemies from {{BD2|Thorns}}.

== Trivia ==
* '''Turret Operator and Living Shield''' appear to be designed in reference to Slay the Spire 1's {{M|Centurion}} and {{M|Mystic}}. The two fights' combatants share similar proportions, and both '''Living Shield''' and Centurion employ an additional attack if their smaller companion is killed.

{{Sequel Disambiguation}}
'''Slimes''' are normal {{2|Monsters|Enemies}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}. They come in four varieties: two Leaf Slimes and two Twig Slimes, each in a small (S) and medium (M) size. They appear together in the Slimes encounter and as companions in other Overgrowth encounters.
== Encounters ==
* Easy Slimes: 1 of each (S) Slime, and a Random (M) Slime.
* Hard Slimes: 1 of each Slime variety.
* {{M2|Flyconid}} and a Random (M) Slime.
* {{M2|Slithering Strangler}} and 1 of each (S) Slime.
* {{M2|Slithering Strangler}} and a Random (M) Slime.

{{Sequel Disambiguation}}
'''Slimes''' are normal {{2|Monsters|Enemies}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}. They come in four varieties: two Leaf Slimes and two Twig Slimes, each in a small (S) and medium (M) size. They appear together in the Slimes encounter and as companions in other Overgrowth encounters.
== Encounters ==
* Easy Slimes: 1 of each (S) Slime, and a Random (M) Slime.
* Hard Slimes: 1 of each Slime variety.
* {{M2|Flyconid}} and a Random (M) Slime.
* {{M2|Slithering Strangler}} and 1 of each (S) Slime.
* {{M2|Slithering Strangler}} and a Random (M) Slime.

Cannot use the same move twice in a row.

{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Phrog Parasite
|Image  = StS2_Phrog Parasite.png

'''Phrog Parasite''' is an {{2|Elites|Elite}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Phrog Parasite}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Infect
|Intent = StatusCard
|Effect = Shuffles 3 {{C2|Infection}} into your discard pile.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Lash
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (4;{{Asc2|9|5}}) damage ×4.
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Phrog Parasite alternates between its two moves:
# {{Int2|Phrog Parasite|Infect}}
# {{Int2|Phrog Parasite|Lash}}
# Back to {{Int2|Phrog Parasite|Infect}}, and so on.

When Phrog Parasite dies, {{BD2|Infested}} triggers and 4 {{M|Wriggler|Wrigglers|2}} are summoned. They will be {{KW2|Stunned}} and do nothing on their first turn. The fight continues until all Wrigglers are defeated.

== Notes ==
* Whether the Wrigglers are {{KW2|Stunned}} on the player's next turn depends on if the Phrog Parasite dies during the player turn or the enemy turn:
** If the Phrog Parasite is killed with an Attack card or damage from an Orb, the Wrigglers will be {{KW2|Stunned}} during this turn, ''not'' the player's next turn.
** If the Phrog Parasite dies to {{BD2|Poison}} or {{BD2|Doom}}, then the Wrigglers will have no {{2|Intent}} when spawned. They will be {{KW2|Stunned}} during the player's next turn.
*** This also applies if the Phrog Parasite dies as a result of its own attack, such as by {{BD2|Thorns}} or {{C2|Necro Mastery}}.
<!--
Confirm this is all correct, I've tested but may have missed something or made a mistake
-->
* '''Infections''' deal damage during the player turn, so the damage will activate cards like {{C2|Inferno}} or {{C2|Rupture}}.
* {{C2|Omnislice}} damages the target, then damages all other enemies afterwards. If the first hit kills the '''Phrog Parasite''', then it will spawn '''Wrigglers''' before the card resolves and the Wrigglers will also take damage.

== Useful Cards ==
* Frontloaded damage cards like {{C2|Perfected Strike}}, {{C2|Backstab}}, and {{C2|Defile}} can be useful for taking down the Phrog Parasite before it can create too many Infections. They can also finish off individual Wrigglers quickly.
* {{C2|Deathbringer}}, {{C2|Deadly Poison}}, and other cards which apply {{BD2|Poison}} or {{BD2|Doom}} can gain an extra turn before the Wrigglers attack, if the Phrog Parasite dies to their damage.
* Attacks which target all enemies like {{C2|Dagger Spray}}, {{C2|Bone Shards}}, and {{C2|Whirlwind}} can damage all of the Wrigglers at once.
* {{C2|Inferno}} deals consistent damage to all enemies every turn. It also triggers whenever '''Infections''' deal unblocked damage.
* Cards which can discard, {{KW2|Exhaust}}, or {{KW2|Transform}} '''Infections''', such as {{C2|Burning Pact}} or {{C2|Hidden Daggers}}, can prevent them from dealing damage.
** {{C2|Compact}} and {{C2|Flak Cannon}} are especially noteworthy, since they remove all '''Infections''' in Hand or in all zones, respectively.

== Wriggler ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Wriggler
|Link   = Slay the Spire 2:Phrog Parasite#Wriggler
|Image  = StS2_Wriggler.png
|HP     = 17-21

|Debut  = Overgrowth
|Type   = Normal
}}
'''Wriggler''' is a normal {{2|Enemy}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}. It appears in the {{E2|Dense Vegetation}} event and is also summoned by {{M2|Phrog Parasite}} upon its death.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Wriggler}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Nasty Bite
|Intent = Attack2
|Effect = Deals (6;{{Asc2|9|7}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Wriggle
|Intent = Buff, StatusCard
|Effect = Shuffles 1 {{C2|Infection}} into your discard pile. Gains 2 {{BD2|Strength}}.
|GivesToEnemy = Strength
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Wrigglers alternate between {{Int2|Wriggler|Nasty Bite}} and {{Int2|Wriggler|Wriggle}}. When multiple Wrigglers are present, they start offset from each other: odd-numbered Wrigglers begin with {{Int2|Wriggler|Nasty Bite}} and even-numbered Wrigglers begin with {{Int2|Wriggler|Wriggle}}.

When summoned by {{M2|Phrog Parasite}} (via {{BD2|Infested}}), each Wriggler spends its first turn {{KW2|Stunned}} before beginning its pattern. In the {{E2|Dense Vegetation}} event, 4 Wrigglers appear at once, starting their patterns immediately (not {{KW2|Stunned}}).

{{Clear}}
== Trivia ==
* The {{R2|Paper Phrog}} is likely based on the same type of creature being {{BD2|Infested}} by the Phrog Parasite.

pages.source_text:
The '''Bowlbugs''' are a group of normal {{2|Monsters|Enemies}} found in the {{2|Hive}}. Each encounter features a Bowlbug (Rock) alongside 1 or 2 worker bowlbugs chosen from Egg, Silk, and Nectar types. Individual bowlbugs also appear alongside {{2|Slumbering Beetle}}.

== Bowlbug (Rock) ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Bowlbug (Rock)
|Link   = Slay The Spire 2:Bowlbugs#Bowlbug (Rock)
|Image  = StS2_Bowlbug (Rock).png
|HP     = 45-48
|AscHP  = 46-49
|Powers = {{BD2|Imbalanced}}
|Debut  = Hive
|Type   = Normal
}} 
{{Power Infobox
|Name         = Imbalanced
|Image        = StS2 Icon Imbalanced.png
|Description  = If the enemy's attacks are fully blocked, it becomes {{KW2|Stunned}}.
|Type         = Debuff
|Stacks       = Does not stack
|BetweenTurns = Permanent
|Cap          = 
|GivesToEnemy = Stunned
}}
=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Bowlbug (Rock)}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Headbutt
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (15;{{Asc2|9|16}}) damage.
}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Dizzy
|Intent = Stun
|Effect = Stunned. Does nothing.
}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Uses {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt}} every turn. However, if {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt}}'s damage is fully prevented by a player, the Bowlbug (Rock) becomes {{KW2|Stunned}} and uses {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Dizzy}} on its next turn, then resumes {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt}}.

=== Notes ===
* The in-game description of {{BD2|Imbalanced}} is somewhat misleading. The Bowlbug (Rock) will become {{KW2|Stunned}} as long as the player has at least 1 {{KW2|Block}} and {{Int|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt|Headbutt's|2}} damage is fully prevented. Some other methods of preventing damage are:
** Playing {{BD2|Buffer}}.
** Reducing the Bowlbug (Rock)'s {{BD2|Strength}}.
** Blocking all but 1 damage and preventing that 1 damage with {{R2|Tungsten Rod}}.
* If the Bowlbug (Rock)'s attack damage is reduced to 0 (such as by {{BD2|Mangle}}) but the player has no {{KW2|Block}}, the Bowlbug (Rock) will ''not'' be {{KW2|Stunned}}.
* If {{KW2|Osty}} takes damage from {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt}}, it will not become {{KW2|Stunned}}.
* Since {{BD2|Imbalanced}} is a debuff, {{C2|Misery}} can apply it to other enemies in the fight.
* In {{2|Multiplayer}}, only one player needs to fully block {{Int2|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt}} to {{KW2|Stunned|Stun}} the Bowlbug (Rock).

{{Clear}}

The '''Cultists''' are a pair of normal {{2|Monsters|Enemies}} found in the {{2|Underdocks}}. The encounter consists of a [[Calcified Cultist]] and a [[Damp Cultist]]. Both follow the same pattern: they buff on their first turn, then attack every turn after. == Calcified Cultist == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Calcified Cultist |Link = Slay The Spire 2:Cultists#Calcified Cultist |Image = StS2_Calcified Cultist.png |HP = 38-41 |AscHP = 39-42 |Debut = Underdocks |Type = Normal }} === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Calcified Cultist}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Incantation |Intent = Buff |Effect = Gains 2 {{BD2|Ritual}}. |GivesToEnemy = Ritual }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Dark Strike |Intent = Attack2 |Effect = Deals (9;{{Asc2|9|11}}) damage. }} {{Intents Table/end}} Always uses {{Int2|Calcified Cultist|Incantation}} first, then {{Int2|Calcified Cultist|Dark Strike}} every turn after. === Dialogue === When using {{Int2|Calcified Cultist|Incantation}}.
{{TS||shake|OUR POWER IS UNMATCHED!}}
{{Clear}} == Damp Cultist == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Damp Cultist |Link = Slay The Spire 2:Cultists#Damp Cultist |Image = StS2_Damp Cultist.png |HP = 51-53 |AscHP = 52-54 |Debut = Underdocks |Type = Normal }} === Pattern === {{Intents Table/start|Damp Cultist}} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Incantation |Intent = Buff |Effect = Gains (5;{{Asc2|9|6}}) {{BD2|Ritual}}. |GivesToEnemy = Ritual }} {{Intents Table/row |Name = Dark Strike |Intent = Attack1 |Effect = Deals (1;{{Asc2|9|3}}) damage. }} {{Intents Table/end}} Always uses {{Int2|Damp Cultist|Incantation}} first, then {{Int2|Damp Cultist|Dark Strike}} every turn after. === Dialogue === When using {{Int2|Damp Cultist|Incantation}}.
{{TS||shake|CAW!
CAAAW}}

{{Sequel Disambiguation}}
'''Slimes''' are normal {{2|Monsters|Enemies}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}. They come in four varieties: two Leaf Slimes and two Twig Slimes, each in a small (S) and medium (M) size. They appear together in the Slimes encounter and as companions in other Overgrowth encounters.
== Encounters ==
* Easy Slimes: 1 of each (S) Slime, and a Random (M) Slime.
* Hard Slimes: 1 of each Slime variety.
* {{M2|Flyconid}} and a Random (M) Slime.
* {{M2|Slithering Strangler}} and 1 of each (S) Slime.
* {{M2|Slithering Strangler}} and a Random (M) Slime.

pages.source_text:
{{Event Infobox |Name=The Lantern Key |Image=StS2_Mysterious Knight.png }} {{Small Card Infobox|Lantern Key|2}} {{E2|The Lantern Key}} is an {{2|Event}} found exclusively in the {{2|Hive}}. It is a combat event. The {{C2|Lantern Key}} can be used in the {{E2|War Historian, Repy}} event in Act 3. == Options == {{Frame|Return the Key}} {{TS|positive||Gain 100 Gold.}}
{{Frame|Keep the Key}} Enter combat against a {{2|Mysterious Knight}} for the {{C2|Lantern Key}} card. == Dialogue ==
You come upon a faintly glowing key and go to pick it up. "Been looking all over for that key! Now if you don't mind..." This person looks like bad news but maybe it's not good to be judgy.
{{Frame|Return the Key}}
The stranger thanks you for your help, and rewards you handsomely.
{{Frame|Keep the Key}}
The stranger looks at you menacingly. It seems like only one of you is making it out of here with the key.
== Notes == * If you choose to {{Frame|Keep the Key}}, the {{2|Mysterious Knight}} combat counts as a normal combat encounter for purposes such as {{R2|Prayer Wheel}} and will drop normal combat rewards along with the {{C2|Lantern Key}}. == Mysterious Knight == {{Enemy Infobox |Name = Mysterious Knight |Image = StS2_Mysterious Knight.png |HP = 101 |AscHP = 108 |Powers = {{BD2|Strength}} 6
{{BD2|Plating}} 6 |Debut = Hive |Type = Normal }} '''Mysterious Knight''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} encountered in the {{E2|The Lantern Key}} event.
